name: Mnemonic 300M
about: The second version, with 24 layers. It was pretrained on 10 billion tokens of FineWeb-Edu and then tuned for chat on smol-smoltalk. The weights are int8, which loses almost nothing against full precision at a quarter of the size.

name: Mnemonic 300M, smaller download
about: The same model with int4 weights. The download is 40% smaller and it runs a little faster, but its answers are slightly worse.

name: Mnemonic 755M
about: The newest and biggest version, with 28 layers. It was pretrained on 15 billion tokens of FineWeb-Edu and tuned for chat on smol-smoltalk. It knows more than the 300M and makes fewer mistakes, but the download is two and a half times bigger and it writes less than half as fast.

name: Mnemonic 755M, smaller download
about: The 755M with int4 weights. The download is 38% smaller and it runs a little faster, but its answers are slightly worse.

name: Mnemonic 126M
about: The first version, with 16 layers, pretrained on 5 billion tokens of FineWeb-Edu and tuned on smol-smoltalk. It is smaller than the 300M and about twice as fast.

name: Mnemonic 126M, smaller download
about: The 126M with int4 weights. This is the smallest download.

name: Mnemonic Math
about: A separate version that only does math: the 300M, fine-tuned on about 15 million generated problems that are worked out one small step at a time. It does arithmetic, fractions, decimals, percents, factoring, square roots, equations, inequalities, lines, sequences and word problems, and gets 99.7% of problems it hasn't seen right. It only knows those kinds of problems, though. Ask it anything else and it will still answer, wrongly.

name: Mnemonic Math, smaller download
about: The math model with int4 weights. The download is 38% smaller, and on the same tests it got exactly as many right as the int8 one.
